entries.text: Ossoff leads Collins 72.6% to 27.4% in the Senate race and Bottoms leads Jackson 68.0% to 32.0% for Governor, with about 18% of the expected vote counted (13 of 159 counties) and results unofficial per civicAPI. Every county is still treated as early vote only, and Gwinnett, Fulton, Houston, Barrow and Floyd are the ones running ahead of win pace, while none are behind. Our model projects D+5.8 in the Senate and D+3.8 for Governor, both with about 11 points of uncertainty and a neutral outlook, so this is too early to read as a lead. Cobb, DeKalb, Cherokee and Chatham have reported nothing, and Cobb (win pace 57.8%) and DeKalb (win pace 83.8%) hold the largest uncounted vote. No SAM target district data is in this feed. The down-ballot statewide races show Democrats at 67% to 70%, but they are at 0.1% reporting and carry no signal yet.

Georgia is the only state with data in this snapshot, and it is too early to call. Democrats lead both statewide top-of-ticket races by wide margins with about 18% counted, but that count is early vote from a few counties and our model shows a neutral outlook with roughly 11 points of uncertainty. Nothing is behind win pace so far, and Gwinnett and Fulton are running ahead. There is no data here for the other five states, so no read is possible on them. The most important thing to watch is Cobb and DeKalb, which together hold about 600,000 uncounted votes and have reported nothing.

Georgia is the only state with data in this snapshot, and it is too early to call. Democrats lead both top-of-ticket races by wide margins and every down-ballot statewide race by roughly 27 to 31 points, but the count is early vote only, and our model shows a neutral outlook with roughly 10.6 points of uncertainty. Nothing in Georgia was behind win pace at last check, and Gwinnett and Fulton were running ahead. There is no data here for the other five states, so no read is possible on them. The most important thing to watch is Cobb and DeKalb, which have reported nothing and hold the largest uncounted vote in the state, and whether their returns pull the Democratic margins toward their win paces.

Ossoff leads Collins 65.0% to 35.0% and Bottoms leads Jackson 60.8% to 39.2%, with about 32% of the expected vote counted from 52 of 159 counties. Both are ahead of win pace in most reporting counties (51 of 51 for Senate, 41 ahead and 10 on pace for Governor), with Gwinnett, Fulton, Henry and Paulding adding the most projected net votes and no county trailing. Our model projects D+18.0 in the Senate and D+11.6 for Governor, each with about 9.4 points of uncertainty and a good outlook, up from D+6.9 and D+4.7 and a neutral outlook at the last snapshot, when only 25 counties had reported. Cobb (win pace 57.8%), DeKalb (83.8%) and Cherokee (30.2%) have reported nothing and hold the largest uncounted vote, so the lead is not settled until they come in. No SAM target district data is in this feed. Down-ballot, Democrats lead every statewide race by 20 to 25 points (Miller 61.9% for Attorney General, McLaurin 62.3% for Lieutenant Governor), but those races show only 0.3% reporting and carry no signal yet.

Brown leads Husted 64.6% to 32.4% in the Senate race and Acton leads Ramaswamy 66.4% to 31.6% for Governor, with about 10% of the expected vote counted from 10 of 88 counties. Every county is still treated as likely early vote only, so none is scored against win pace, though all 10 reporting counties are ahead on that basis, led by Franklin, Summit, Stark and Mahoning. Our model projects D+4.0 in the Senate and D+4.5 for Governor, each with about 11.9 points of uncertainty and a neutral outlook. Cuyahoga (win pace 71.0%), Hamilton (62.4%) and Montgomery (55.5%) have reported nothing and hold much of the remaining vote. No SAM target district data is in this feed. Down-ballot, Democrats lead the Attorney General, Supreme Court, Secretary of State and Treasurer races by roughly 32 to 36 points at under 4% reporting, and State Issue 3 (photo ID to vote) has Yes ahead 53.1% to 46.9% at 4.8% reporting.

Georgia looks good: Ossoff and Bottoms lead comfortably with about 32% counted, no county is behind win pace, and our model is at D+18.0 and D+11.6 with a good outlook. Ohio is too early: Brown and Acton lead big, but only about 10% is counted, all of it treated as early vote, and our model outlook is neutral at D+4.0 and D+4.5. The feed has no data for the other four states, so no read is possible on them. Down-ballot leads in both states are large but come from under 5% reporting in most races and mean little yet. The most important thing to watch is whether Cobb and DeKalb in Georgia and Cuyahoga and Hamilton in Ohio, none of which has reported, come in near their win paces as the early-vote-only leads get tested.

Ossoff leads Collins 63.3% to 36.7% with 31.7% reporting, and NBC News and Decision Desk HQ have called the Senate race for Ossoff. Bottoms leads Jackson 59.1% to 40.9% in the Governor race, which is not called. Ossoff is ahead of win pace in all 71 scored counties. Bottoms is ahead in 51 and on pace in 20, with none behind, and Gwinnett, Fulton, Henry, Paulding and Chatham add the most projected net votes. Our model has D+18.3 for the Senate and D+11.8 for Governor, both with a good outlook. Since the last snapshot, reporting counties rose from 52 to 72 and the model barely moved, while the leads narrowed slightly (Ossoff from 65.0%, Bottoms from 60.8%). Cobb, DeKalb and Cherokee still have nothing in and hold the largest uncounted vote. There is no SAM target district data in this feed. Down-ballot Democrats lead every statewide race by roughly 17 to 22 points, but those races are at 0.6% reporting and carry no signal yet.

Brown leads Husted 62.7% to 34.2% with 24% reporting, and Acton leads Ramaswamy 64.3% to 33.5% with 23.9% reporting. Win pace is not yet a real test, because every county is still treated as likely early vote only: 40 counties are ahead on that basis for the Senate and 44 for Governor, with Franklin, Hamilton, Cuyahoga, Montgomery and Summit adding the most projected net votes. Our model has D+9.2 for the Senate (neutral outlook) and D+10.1 for Governor (good outlook), up from D+4.0 and D+4.5 at the last snapshot when 10 counties had reported, and 45 of 88 have now reported. The SAM target OH-07 has Poindexter at 69.4% to Miller's 30.6% with 21% reporting. Only Cuyahoga and Wayne are in, Medina and Ashland have reported nothing, and our model has D+9.2 with a neutral outlook and wide uncertainty. Down-ballot Democrats lead Attorney General, Supreme Court and Secretary of State by roughly 27 to 29 points at under 18% reporting, and State Issue 3 (photo ID) has Yes ahead 53.2% to 46.8% at 18.7% reporting.

Georgia looks good: Ossoff's Senate win is called, Bottoms leads for Governor with no county behind win pace, and our model has D+18.3 and D+11.8. Ohio is still early: Brown and Acton lead by large margins, but the counted vote is early-vote heavy, every county is scored on that basis only, and our model is neutral for the Senate at D+9.2 and good for Governor at D+10.1. The OH-07 SAM target shows Poindexter well ahead, but Medina and Ashland have not reported and our model outlook there is neutral. The feed has no data for the other four states, so no read is possible on them. The most important thing to watch is Ohio's large uncounted vote in Franklin, Cuyahoga and Hamilton as it moves from early-vote-only scoring to real win-pace comparisons, with Cobb and DeKalb in Georgia the matching test for Bottoms.

Ossoff leads Collins 61.8% to 38.2% in the Senate race with 38.9% reporting, and NBC News and Decision Desk HQ have called it for Ossoff; Bottoms leads Jackson 57.6% to 42.4% for Governor, not called. Ossoff is ahead of win pace in 87 counties and on pace in 2, with none behind, while Bottoms is ahead in 68, on pace in 20 and behind in 1, with Gwinnett, Fulton, Henry, Cherokee and Paulding adding the most projected net votes. Our model has D+19.3 for the Senate and D+12.5 for Governor, both with a good outlook, and Cobb and DeKalb still have nothing in and hold the largest uncounted vote. There is no SAM target district data in this feed. Down-ballot Democrats lead every statewide race by roughly 15 to 19 points, but those races are at 0.9% reporting and carry no signal yet. Since the last snapshot, reporting counties rose from 72 to 90 and our model moved up slightly, while the leads narrowed slightly (Ossoff from 63.3%, Bottoms from 59.1%).

Brown leads Husted 60.5% to 36.3% in the Senate race with 28.7% reporting, and Acton leads Ramaswamy 61.7% to 36.0% for Governor with 29.2% reporting; neither is called. Win pace is not yet a real test, because every county is still treated as likely early vote only: 53 counties are ahead on that basis for the Senate and 62 for Governor, with Franklin, Hamilton, Cuyahoga, Montgomery and Summit adding the most projected net votes. Our model has D+10.4 for the Senate and D+11.7 for Governor, both with a good outlook. The SAM target OH-07 has Poindexter at 66.3% to Miller's 33.7% with 23.6% reporting; Cuyahoga, Wayne and Ashland are in, Medina has nothing yet, and our model has D+9.9 with a neutral outlook and wide uncertainty. Down-ballot, Democrats lead Attorney General, both Supreme Court races, Secretary of State and Treasurer by roughly 21 to 23 points at about 24 to 26% reporting, and State Issue 3 (photo ID) has Yes ahead 55.1% to 44.9% at 27.5% reporting. Since the last snapshot, Brown and Acton's leads have narrowed, the Senate outlook has moved from neutral to good, and 61 to 65 counties have now reported.

Ossoff leads Collins 61.5% to 38.5% in the Senate race with 46.3% reporting, and NBC News and Decision Desk HQ have called it for him. Down-ballot, Democrats lead Attorney General 59.1% to 40.9% at 30.8% reporting, Supreme Court 59.6% to 40.4% at 30.7%, and Treasurer 58.8% to 41.2% at 32.6%. State Issue 3 (photo ID) has Yes ahead 56.1% to 43.9% at 31.6% reporting. There is no SAM target district data in this feed. Michigan is at 0.6% reporting, so this is a first read with little weight. El-Sayed leads Rogers 76.0% to 22.0% for Senate and Benson leads James 78.4% to 20.5% for Governor, with only 2 of 83 counties in. Both counties are ahead of win pace, led by Kent, and our model has D+2.8 for the Senate and D+3.0 for Governor, both neutral with about 13 points of uncertainty. Oakland, Wayne and Macomb have nothing in and hold the largest uncounted vote. There is no SAM target district data in this feed, and down-ballot races are at 0% reporting, though Proposal 2 shows Yes at 88.5% on early numbers.

Talarico leads Paxton 60.5% to 38.0% for Senate with 22.7% reporting, and Hinojosa leads Abbott 53.3% to 45.5% for Governor with 17.3% reporting. No county is yet ahead of win pace on actual votes: for the Senate 6 counties are on pace and 8 are ahead on likely early vote only, and for Governor 14 are on pace, none behind, with Tarrant, Fort Bend and Williamson adding the most projected net votes on early vote only. Our model has D+4.0 for the Senate and D+1.6 for Governor, both neutral with about 10 points of uncertainty. Harris, Bexar, Travis and Collin have nothing in. The SAM target TX-34 has Gonzalez at 49.3% to Flores's 46.4% with 26.3% reporting. Down-ballot races are at 2 to 3% reporting, with Democrats ahead in each.

Ossoff leads Collins 63.8% to 36.2% for Senate with 53.1% reporting, and NBC News and Decision Desk HQ have called it for him. Bottoms leads Jackson 59.6% to 40.4% for Governor at 53%. Both are well ahead of win pace: 105 counties are ahead on the Senate race, and Gwinnett, Cobb, Fulton and DeKalb add the most projected net votes. Cooper leads Whatley 66.4% to 32.0% for Senate with 52.1% reporting. Cooper is ahead of win pace in all 62 reporting counties, led by Wake, Mecklenburg, Guilford, Forsyth and Buncombe, and our model has D+24.1 with a good outlook. Johnston and Randolph have nothing in yet, and Wake and Mecklenburg hold the most uncounted vote. The SAM target NC-11 has Ager at 63.7% to Balkcom's 35.3% with 68.8% reporting. Our model has D+21.7 there, good, with all 12 reporting counties ahead of win pace, and Jackson and Cherokee still empty.

This feed has no Senate or Governor totals and no county win-pace model for Ohio, so there is no read on the top of the ticket or on win pace. The one race in the feed is Treasurer, where Walsh (D) leads Edwards (R) 58.0% to 42.0% with 35.5% reporting. There is no SAM target district data in this feed. Since the last snapshot, Treasurer reporting rose from 32.6% to 35.5% and the Democratic lead narrowed from 58.8% to 58.0%.

Michigan is early at 6.5% reporting. El-Sayed leads Rogers 57.5% to 40.9% for Senate and Benson leads James 61.0% to 37.7% for Governor, with 5 to 6 of 83 counties in. Kent and Oakland are ahead of win pace, Ottawa and Eaton trail, and our model has D+2.8 for Senate and D+4.8 for Governor, both neutral with about 12 points of uncertainty. Wayne, Macomb and Washtenaw have nothing in, and Wayne holds about 595,000 votes left. The SAM target MI-10 has Bouchard (R) at 52.9% to Hines (D) at 45.1% with 3.3% reporting, and our model has R+2.0, neutral, with only Oakland counted and trailing pace. Since the last snapshot, the Senate lead narrowed from 76.0% to 57.5% as reporting rose from 0.6% to 6.5%, and our model moved from D+2.8 to D+2.8 for Senate and D+3.0 to D+4.8 for Governor.

The SAM target TX-34 has Gonzalez (D) at 49.3% to Flores (R) at 46.4% with 26.3% reporting, a 2.9-point lead. Down-ballot, Democrats lead Attorney General 59.3% to 39.4%, Comptroller 58.1% to 39.7% and Lieutenant Governor 58.6% to 39.3%, all at about 3% reporting and likely early vote. The Court of Criminal Appeals, Land Commissioner and Supreme Court races are at 0 to 3.3% reporting and carry little signal. Georgia looks good, though the statewide down-ballot races are too early to read. Tanya Miller (D) leads Attorney General 59.2% to 40.8%, McLaurin leads Lieutenant Governor 59.6% to 40.4%, Hubbard leads Public Service Commission 3 59.9% to 40.1%, and Powell leads State Superintendent 58.2% to 41.8%, all at only 2.5% reporting. North Carolina has no top-of-ticket totals in this feed, so the read comes from the SAM target districts. NC-11 is the strong one: Ager (D) leads Balkcom 60.8% to 38.0% with 81.1% reporting, all 15 reporting counties are ahead of win pace, and our model has D+20.8 with a good outlook, driven by Buncombe, Henderson and Haywood. Cherokee has nothing in yet, and Buncombe has about 20,000 votes left. NC-05 is closer: Hubbard (D) leads Foxx 55.6% to 42.3% with 48.4% reporting, 5 counties are ahead of win pace and 2 are on it, and our model has D+4.1 with about 7 points of uncertainty, neutral. Guilford and Rockingham drive the lead there, but Rockingham, Guilford, Caldwell, Alexander and Ashe hold the most uncounted vote, and Alexander and Ashe are still empty with GOP-leaning win paces. Since the last snapshot, Ager's share fell from 63.7% to 60.8% as reporting rose from 68.8% to 81.1%, and our model moved from D+21.7 to D+20.8.

Michigan is early at 8.5% reporting. Benson (D) leads James 58.6% to 40.1% for Governor and El-Sayed (D) leads Rogers 55.5% to 42.9% for Senate, with our model at D+3.9 and D+2.0, both neutral with about 12 points of uncertainty. The SAM target MI-10 has Bouchard (R) at 53.6% to Hines (D) at 44.4% with 5.7% reporting, and our model has R+3.2, neutral, with only Oakland counted and trailing pace and Macomb still empty.
